newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Cisneros ends deal with Coke - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Cisneros ends deal with Coke - newspaper.

text.p: Venezuela's Cisneros Group has decided to sell its 50 percent stake in a soft drink bottling venture with Coca-Cola Co in Venezuela to a Colombian company, leading daily El Universal reported on Saturday.
The move, which industry analysts had been expected for weeks, meant the complete withdrawal of the leading business family Cisneros from the soft drink business.
El Universal gave no figures for the deal with Panamco- Indega, a subsidiary of Mexican bottler Panamerican Beverages (Panamco), the largest Coca Cola bottler in Latin America, including Colombia.
The information could no be immediately confirmed with Grupo Cisneros Embotelladoras de Venezuela.
The joint venture between Cisneros and Coke had been formed last August to run 18 bottling plants and a fleet of 2,500 trucks under the name of Embotelladoras Coca Cola y Hit de Venezuela.

The deal with Coca-Cola attracted interest as it abruptly ended Grupo Cisneros' 50-year-old collaboration with PepsiCo. The two partners were later fined $1.9 million for forming a venture that violated Venezuela's anti-trust regulations. But Venezuela's anti-monopoly commission (Procompetencia) did not block the venture.

The defection of the Cisneros group, with wide interests in telecommunications and television, dealt a strong blow to Pepsi's plans in Latin America. Pepsi later signed a bottling deal with local powerful foods and beverage company Polar.
